what: A wordmark built from square pieces stretches to fit the panel size. The farther a letter is from the lens focus, the wider it gets, and the closer, the narrower (difference from the average distance × 1.6, narrowest .15x). Vertically it bends around the focus height so the cells near the focus grow (1/(1+1.4) squared). With follow: cursor the focus trails the mouse, covering 1 − .88^dt of the remaining distance each frame. With loop it travels straight between the four corners (.98·.02 → .98·.98 → .02·.98 → .02·.02) at .7s each — the full-bleed logo on the end screen and the ”Desktop only” screen

options.follow: cursor (default, loop on touch devices) | loop | none
options.spread: How far letter spacing spreads with distance, default 1.6 — 0 keeps it even
options.bend: Vertical bend, default 1.4 — 0 keeps it straight
options.each: Length (s) of one corner step in loop, default .7
options.lag: Ratio kept from the cursor each frame, default .88 (higher follows more slowly)
options.box: Board size the piece coordinates are written on (‹width height›), fits to the edges of the pieces if omitted
options.[data-fx-part=module]: One piece — data-rect="x y w h"(panel coordinates), the same letter name in data-letter (grouped so they widen together)

use: …
note: The text piece is drawn in with the user’s own logo (the demo uses a placeholder TITLE). When the panel is flat (a band), the text gets squashed and looks like vertical bars — that is also faithful to the original. The formula was measured from the original and rewritten.
